notes: Robinhood Chain, chain id 4663. SovrnToken (SOVRN.ONE / SVO, 18 decimals) has no constructor arguments and no owner, mint, tax, pause or blacklist; its whole supply is minted once to its deployer. SovrnHook's constructor is (IPoolManager, SovrnToken, address factory) in that order, written $poolManager, $token, $factory; it has no owner argument. Its five permissions encode flags 8396 (0x20cc); getHookPermissions returns exactly them and PrepareLaunch.mine finds a matching CREATE2 salt. Callbacks are PoolManager-only. beforeInitialize accepts one initialization, only from the factory, only for {IMD, SVO} at fee 12500 with this hook and a positive tick spacing, at whatever opening price the factory derives from policy; pool.initialPrice here is the nominal one-to-one value, not an instruction. The constructor deploys the immutable LifeForceVault (vault()). Fees are paid in IMD to the vault: sells 3.5%; buys 50% at pool opening decaying linearly to 3.5% over 3600 seconds; taken directly when the manager holds the IMD, else as an ERC-6909 claim anyone may redeemFees() to the vault. The vault has no owner or setters; only the Safe 0xeb57c52272b90f989c41b739e2ccc5f00bf7697c may withdraw (70% inference / 30% buyback of received IMD), to itself only; burn() sends the vault's SVO to the dead address. Liquidity operations and other pools pay no hook fee. Review of the code as it is (no source changed; forge test: 173 passed, 2 skipped, the fork test needs FORK_4663_RPC). BLOCKING: the hook constructor reverts unless block.chainid == 4663 and IMD has code, and LifeForceVault repeats the IMD code check. The admission floor (Hook.protected.t.sol) deploys the attested creation code in setUp on a local EVM with the default chain id and no code at IMD, so CREATE2 returns zero and setUp fails with 'hook deployment reverted' for every floor test. Reproduced by running a copy of the floor with the probe environment; with chain id 4663 and code at IMD etched before deployment the same four floor tests pass and the token floor passes 7 of 7, so the gates are the only blocker. Fix (a src change, not done here): drop the chain-id check and both IMD code checks from the constructors; beforeInitialize already binds the pair. MEDIUM (reproduced, not fixed, disclosed in README): with no liquidity callbacks, an IMD-only position just above the price converts IMD to SVO through sell flow and pays no hook fee. At opening, 59052891958053492 wei IMD placed as a position returned 61732429133889101342956 wei SVO after a 5,000,000 SVO sell, fee 0, while a direct buy of the same IMD paid 29526445979026746 wei (50%) and returned 29072597369812571613728 wei SVO. Closing it needs liquidity hooks and changes flags 8396; the launch owner decides. Fixed in this manifest: notes were 4042 characters; pairedCurrency is now lowercase; initialPrice is the launch's nominal value (the previous value assumed a 3,000 IMD cap with IMD as currency0; launch-attestation.json still records that value). Because script/attest.py hard-codes the previous checksummed pairedCurrency and initialPrice and hashes launch.json, attest.py --check now fails on the pool block; that script and launch-attestation.json are outside this task's write scope and need regenerating by their owner. Trust assumptions outside this code: IMD's single owner key can enable a v4 transfer gate that would stop this pool's swaps and liquidity moves, and as a LayerZero OFT can in effect mint IMD; the real PoolManager's owner can set a protocol fee; the Safe's signing threshold (2 of 3 when read on 2026-10-09) is the only control over collected fees. Routers that pay IMD before swapping must add the buy fee. Not audited; no claim of security.
